slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
"You sit all day, so your hip flexors are short." Heard that one?

Research suggests sitting doesn't usually shorten muscles in a lasting way. Many desk workers test with normal hip flexor length yet still feel tight at the front of the hip. The feeling is real, but it's often driven by staying still and low activity.

What tends to help more than endless stretching: moving often and strengthening your hips and glutes. Try five slow lunges each side, ten bridges and a short walk every hour or so.

Groin pain that catches, a limp or pain at night is worth an assessment. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio.
